about: Suite v1's tasks (SPEC-011 4.4), drafted from Freeflow's own merged pull requests: each starts at its merge's first parent, asks for the change as Hassan would, and is checked by the pull request's own tests at its merge, held back from the workspace. scripts/groups.mjs writes the groups, graders and cards from this file. size: fix (one Slice), feature (several Slices, a compaction likely on a long run), long (a long task a coordinator would delegate parts of). Drafted by the build; Hassan prunes them.

tasks.prompt: Task records written before we switched to the one Recovery list can't be recovered anymore: every Track Work command refuses them because they still have Defined by, Read on recovery, Read when and Carry lines. Can you make migrate convert those records?
preferences: migrate converts such a record in place, and keeps the old record whole in the task folder as sources/record-before-recovery.md.
Defined by lines become `always, not counted` Recovery lines, Read on recovery lines become `always`, Read when lines become `when <trigger>`, and the files a Carry line named become `always` lines.
Every other line of the record stays as it was, and the other commands keep refusing an unconverted record, saying to run migrate.
required: migrate converts a Schema 4 record in place, keeping the old record whole and every closed Slice in History
migrate --project copies the task into the store as its next task, converts it there and commits, leaving the original as it was
migrate --project brings a Schema 5 task kept in a repository into the store, unchanged, leaving the original (P91)
migrate refuses a cue that is not one and a cue for a Slice that is not closed, writing nothing
migrate converts a Schema 5 record written before the one Recovery list, keeping the old record and every other line

tasks.prompt: The planner prices every Slice at roughly Opus prices because it takes the median over all past Slices, whatever model they ran on, so a Haiku Slice gets a cost way too high. Can you make a Slice's predicted cost come from past Slices run on its own model and effort?
preferences: The model and effort are the ones of the transcript's newest request when the Slice starts (and for estimate --plan).
Use the Slices run mostly on that model and effort once there are at least three of them; otherwise fall back to all of them, and say on the Predicted line which one the cost came from.
Context and working time stay pooled over every model; only the cost is per model.
A prediction whose cost came from a different model than its Slice actually ran on should not be used to correct later costs.
required: a Slice's prediction: the median of the first pool with three measured Slices, corrected by the geometric mean of actual over predicted, pulled toward none (P16)
slice start records the prediction beside the first reading, and slice close keeps it beside the actual
a Slice's cost comes from Slices run on its model and effort once three are measured, else from all, naming the model most of it was measured on; context and time from all (P8 of A-005)
a prediction whose cost was measured on another model than its Slice ran on corrects its context and time, not later costs
slice start and estimate --plan price by the model and effort of the transcript's newest request
estimate --plan lays the Slices left across compaction cycles, with the totals, the oversized and the parallel
estimate --plan before three Slices are measured anywhere: this compaction cycle's rate, from --done
Slices measured with --used carry context only: the prediction and the plan give no time or cost for them
estimate --project and --store add up what was measured, and size a task with nothing measured from others' data
a sized Slice: its files times the median per-file rate, corrected only by sized predictions, and a zero reading is not measured (P13 to P18)
slice start writes Size and Base, slice close writes Files from Base to HEAD, and slice size adds Files to an older Slice

tasks.prompt: Every time I change code a dev doc covers, I have to bump its Verified at by hand, and that often ends up as a separate commit. Can docs-check move a stale document's Verified at itself? And while you're there, CI runs every check and test suite one after another, which takes almost 5 minutes; can you split the tests into parallel shards?
preferences: docs-check.mjs <docs> --stamp moves each stale document's Verified at to HEAD with today's date, so it goes into the same commit as the code.
Feature files are never stamped: only driving them moves their Verified at.
The test shards must cover every suite npm test lists, so none can be left out, and the required Deterministic checks job passes only when all of them did.

tasks.prompt: Research Work's guidance asks for three things its checks don't actually check: a claim that something is new should cite the search behind it, every analysis variant a study plan lists should get reported, and a plan should declare the models in its method with exact snapshots. Can you add those checks?
preferences: Claims of novelty are found by wording class (being first, nobody or nothing having done it, words that say new), not by a fixed phrase list, and ordinal uses like "the first study arm" are left alone.
A variant counts as reported only where a row names it as "variant V<n>".
A Models row needs a listed role, an exact snapshot (never latest) and a real date no later than today; study.mjs check notes a plan that declares no models.

tasks.prompt: Research Work can't aggregate results over several seeds and tasks yet. Can you add aggregates: the interquartile mean, mean, median and optimality gap with stratified bootstrap intervals, the probability that one method beats another, and an interval for pass^k for one task or a whole suite?
preferences: The suite pass^k interval resamples tasks and then each drawn task's trials at its observed rate, not tasks alone, which leaves the trial noise out.
Below 10 tasks the result warns; aggregates and the probability of improvement warn when a task has one run or fewer than 5.
resamples must be a whole number of at least 1; null means the default.
required: the point estimates follow their definitions
the stratified bootstrap resamples runs within each task, never across tasks

the command line runs the aggregate family and the pass^k intervals
the bootstrap intervals match exact enumeration of every resample on small designs
a suite's pass^k interval resamples trials within tasks too, and warns when tasks are few
degenerate designs and odd inputs are named, never silently wrong

tasks.prompt: Delegations for Schema 5 tasks are all kept by hand right now: writing the brief, making the worker's worktree, recording it, checking and closing the return. Can you add delegate commands to Track Work's script for that?
preferences: delegate open assigns D-NNN, writes brief.md from the template in delegations/D-NNN-<slug>/, makes a writing worker's worktree on its own branch at the base, and writes the delegation's line in Current Work's Delegations.
open --parent opens a sub-worker's delegation inside its worker's folder and refuses a fourth level.

delegate amend appends a dated change; status lists the open delegations with their sub-workers; check-return refuses a missing return, State or heading, and a commit not on the brief's branch, then marks the line returned.

close records the outcome, model, effort, tokens, minutes, merge commit and return in one History entry and removes the line; view recover --delegation prints the worker's rule, brief, progress and return first.
required: delegate open writes the brief, makes the worker's worktree on its own branch at the base, and writes the delegation's line
delegate amend appends a dated change and records the handle; a returned delegation runs again

delegate is for Schema 5 records

tasks.prompt: After a compaction the agent keeps re-running the same commands to see their output again. Pi's context reuse carries tool results across a compaction; can Track Work do that too, with a task or without one?
preferences: carry list numbers this compaction cycle's tool results from the session's transcript, each with its time, what the call was for, its size and its ID; carry show prints one whole.
In flight's `- Carry: result <n> — <why>` carries one, and checkpoint pins it to its tool-use ID.
The bundle carries those results whole, then adds this cycle's newest other results within a carry budget of 15% of the window, at most 40,000 tokens, and lists older ones by ID.
A session summary takes the same Carry lines, so it works with no task.

tasks.prompt: The planner predicts every Slice as the median one, so a one-line fix and a 200-file removal get the same figures. Can you size each Slice by the files it will touch when planning?
preferences: A Slice carries `Size: <n> files`; slice start records Base (the work repository and its commit), and slice close writes Files, the files added, changed or renamed from Base to HEAD. slice size gives an older Slice its Files.
A sized Slice is predicted as its size times the median per-file rate of the nearest pool with three sized Slices, with the range from the lowest and highest rate.
A reading that found no requests is not a Slice that used nothing.

tasks.prompt: Two problems since task records moved into the store. An entry under Defined by or Read on recovery that names no file gets a line in the checks instead of being dropped silently.

tasks.prompt: Freeflow's mod on Claude Code compacts on its own once a checkpoint is done after the notice, sometimes in the middle of finished work it wanted to keep, or right before a pause. I'd rather the agent ask for the compaction explicitly. Can you add checkpoint --compact for that?
preferences: checkpoint --compact (with --record or --session) leaves a request in the store's sessions/<session>/compact.json, which session status reports.
The mod answers it once, when the turn ends: it marks the request done, runs /compact, which installs the bundle, and submits a prompt to continue.

Nothing else makes the mod compact: the 75% notice only reminds the agent to checkpoint with --compact, and a checkpoint without it never compacts. My own /compact and Claude's own compaction stay as they are.
required: session status prints this session's state in the store as JSON: its task, its summary, unsynced changes and its transcript

tasks.prompt: I'd like Research Work to recheck the numbers another study reports: whether a mean, a percentage or an SD is even possible for its sample size, and whether a p value follows from its test statistic. Can you add that?
preferences: A Recheck Table holds one reported result per row, its values labelled and each number copied as printed; stats.mjs recheck computes each row and writes its Status, so only the computation writes a verdict.

A search too large to run is not computable, never a pass.
The Track Work validate test that puts part of HEAD into a Result line should use the full hash, since an all-digit prefix sometimes isn't counted as a commit.

tasks.prompt: Freeflow on Codex only delivers its session-start guidance. Can you write a Freeflow driver for Codex that does what Codex's hooks allow, like the mod does on Claude Code?
preferences: hooks/codex/driver.mjs answers every Codex hook event Freeflow uses: the guidance and the task menu at session start (fork included), context rows and the notice from each model request's token usage, the task's bundle after Codex compacts, the event log flushed at a turn's end, the store synced, and the hold released at the session's end.
Its claims: pin, inject, checkpoint and sensors yes; block possible until the gates join PreToolUse; the rest no.
Codex gives SessionEnd almost no time, so task release --no-push commits the release here only and the next store sync pushes it.
Schema v1 of the event log takes Codex's lines.

redaction replaces keys and tokens in a command before it is written
events append sets seq per log under a lock, redacts and cuts commands, and refuses what is not schema v1
two writers of one log never share a seq; a stale lock is cleared, a live one makes the batch fail
the event log stays out of the store's Git, and a home with only a log still takes a store
checkpoint and release commit the session's event summary since it took the task

a session holds one task at a time: take refuses a second, switch releases the first
